planting.note: Divide established clumps in early spring or plant container stock into moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, where the purple foliage flush intensifies with cooler temperatures.

directions: Purpurteppich is a selected form of the Pacific Northwest woodland native fringecups, chosen for the deep purple-bronze wash that develops across its rounded, hairy, heuchera-like leaves, an effect most pronounced during cool spring and autumn weather and in winters mild enough for the semi-evergreen foliage to persist. In late spring it sends up the same slender, upright flower wands as the species, each lined with small, fringed, greenish-cream blooms that age toward pink, held above the colored foliage mat. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; too much direct sun bleaches the purple tone and can scorch the thin leaves, while deeper shade favors foliage color over dense flowering. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to renew vigor and control the modest self-seeding typical of the species.
